es: Defender una postura en un panel sobre movilidad urbana: apertura, concesión, refutación con evidencia y cierre con síntesis.

vocabulary.es: compensación, equilibrio entre ventajas y costes

teaching.en: The chair opens the panel, introduces each panellist and reminds everyone that the debate concerns urban mobility, not personal attacks.
teaching.es: El moderador abre el panel, presenta a cada panelista y recuerda a todos que el debate trata de la movilidad urbana, no de ataques personales.
teaching.explanationEs: Panel = mesa de debate; panellist = quien participa en ella; chair = quien la preside.

everyone that the debate concerns urban mobility, not personal attacks.

teaching.en: Each panellist begins with an opening statement of one minute that sets out a position and promises at least two supporting reasons.
teaching.es: Cada panelista empieza con una declaración de apertura de un minuto que expone una postura y promete al menos dos razones que la apoyan.
teaching.explanationEs: La apertura da tu postura y anuncia tus razones; sets out = expone con claridad.

sets out a position and promises at least two supporting reasons.

teaching.en: Granted, congestion is a problem, but free buses would cost too much and may not prove viable for a city of this size.
teaching.es: Es cierto que la congestión es un problema, pero los autobuses gratuitos costarían demasiado y quizá no resultarían viables en una ciudad de este tamaño.
teaching.explanationEs: La concesión (granted) y la réplica (but) son las dos mitades de un turno; viable = realizable en la práctica.
segments: Granted, congestion is a problem, but free buses would cost too much
and may not prove viable for a city of this size.

teaching.en: Pedestrian streets make the centre safer, hence the support of parents, yet every such scheme involves a trade-off with local traders.
teaching.es: Las calles peatonales hacen el centro más seguro, de ahí el apoyo de los padres, pero todo plan así implica una compensación con los comerciantes locales.
teaching.explanationEs: Hence conecta la razón con la consecuencia en registro formal; trade-off = ventajas que se ganan y costes que se aceptan.

teaching.en: The panellist concedes one point and then offers a rebuttal, arguing that the benefits of a car-free centre outweigh the lost parking income.
teaching.es: El panelista concede un punto y luego ofrece una refutación, argumentando que los beneficios de un centro sin autos superan los ingresos perdidos por estacionamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: La refutación es tu contraargumento, apoyado en datos; outweigh = pesar más que.

teaching.en: On balance, an urban plan should tackle traffic without harming shops, which is why the closing statement must weigh both sides.
teaching.es: En conjunto, un plan urbano debe abordar el tráfico sin perjudicar a las tiendas, por eso la declaración de cierre debe sopesar ambos lados.
teaching.explanationEs: On balance abre el cierre con síntesis: sopesa los dos lados; tackle = abordar un problema.

prompt.es: Lee las instrucciones. ¿Qué debe incluir una buena declaración de apertura?

choices.text: A clear position followed by two main reasons.
A concession followed by a long personal anecdote.
A summary of both sides followed by a vote.

feedback.es: La apertura da tu postura y anuncia dos razones; concesión, anécdotas y resumen llegan después.

hint.es: Piensa en qué pide la presidenta al empezar: postura y razones.

origin.text: The chair says: 'You have one minute for your opening statement. Begin with your position, then give your two main reasons.'

prompt.es: Completa: «…dudo que un plan así sea viable en una ciudad de este tamaño.»

feedback.es: Viable describe un plan que se puede llevar a la práctica con los medios disponibles.

hint.es: Adjetivo para un plan que puede realizarse en la práctica.

origin.text: Free buses would be welcome, of course, but I doubt that such a plan is ___ for a city of this size.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En conjunto, los beneficios superan los costes.»

answer.text: On balance, the benefits outweigh the costs

feedback.es: On balance abre el cierre sopesando ambos lados y outweigh expresa que los beneficios pesan más.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula de cierre On balance.

prompt.es: Escucha el comienzo del panel y elige qué concede la comerciante.

choices.text: That pedestrian streets make the centre safer.
That congestion is a real problem.
That families prefer a centre without cars.

feedback.es: La comerciante dice «granted, congestion is a problem» y replica con la caída de sus ingresos; lo demás lo defiende el urbanista.

origin.audio: At the start of the panel, the chair introduced three speakers on urban mobility. The first panellist, a shopkeeper, opposed pedestrian streets: granted, congestion is a problem, but her takings fell sharply when a nearby street closed. The second, a city planner, answered that the trade-off is worth it, since pedestrian streets make the centre safer and, hence, better for families. The chair then asked both to tackle the same question: who should pay?

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige cómo responde el urbanista a la comerciante.

choices.text: He denies that any shop lost money when the street closed.
He agrees with her and proposes to reopen the street.
He argues that safer streets bring families, which justifies the cost.

feedback.es: El urbanista acepta el coste (trade-off) pero sostiene que calles más seguras traen familias, y eso lo compensa.

prompt.es: Escucha la intervención y elige qué postura defiende la oradora.

choices.text: That the centre should be free of cars at weekends.
That traders should decide the opening hours of the centre.
That the centre should be free of cars every day.

feedback.es: Su postura es que el centro no tenga autos los fines de semana (car-free at weekends).

origin.audio: I would like to begin by thanking the chair. My position is simple: our centre should be car-free at weekends. Admittedly, some traders fear losing customers. Even so, cities that have tried it report more visitors, not fewer, and shops that adapted their opening hours did better than before.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez: ¿qué deja entrever sobre las tiendas que adaptaron sus horarios?

choices.text: That opening hours matter more than the cars themselves.
That the fear of losing customers is often overstated.
That traders were right to fear losing their customers.

feedback.es: Si las tiendas que adaptaron sus horarios mejoraron, el miedo a perder clientes suele estar exagerado.

feedback.es: On balance es la fórmula fija para sopesar ambos lados y llegar a una conclusión.

origin.text: Pedestrian streets may cost some shops customers; ___ balance, however, they make the centre safer for everyone.

prompt.es: Escribe tu turno en el panel: apertura, concesión, refutación y cierre.

answer.text: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. Hence the growing support among parents, who want safer streets for their children. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. In so doing, the council would show that it listens to both sides. To sum up, we should tackle traffic now, before urban life becomes impossible. Thank you.
accepted: Thank you, chair. My position is clear: the city centre should be closed to cars at weekends. Granted, congestion is a real problem, and some shops fear that they will lose customers. Nonetheless, the evidence from other cities suggests that pedestrian streets bring more visitors, thereby helping shops rather than harming them. Hence the growing support among parents, who want safer streets for their children. With respect, my opponent says that free buses would be a better solution, but that plan would cost too much and may not prove viable. Admittedly, a car-free centre involves a trade-off, yet on balance the benefits outweigh the costs. A scheme whereby residents keep access to their homes would protect the people who live here. In so doing, the council would show that it listens to both sides. To sum up, we should tackle traffic now, before urban life becomes impossible. Thank you.

Thank you, chair. I am against a full ban on cars in the centre, and I would like to explain why. To be fair, my opponent is right that congestion is a problem, and I would not deny that pedestrian streets are safer. That said, the evidence from our own city shows that shops lost much of their takings when a nearby street closed. Hence the concern of traders, who cannot wait for years to see whether visitors return. Even so, I am willing to concede that some streets could close, thereby giving families more space. A scheme whereby residents and traders vote street by street would be more viable than a single decision for the whole centre. With respect, a trade-off that ignores the people who work here is not a fair one. On balance, I believe that we should test one street first and tackle congestion step by step. Thank you.

feedback.es: Un buen turno encadena postura, concesión, refutación con evidencia y conector formal, y cierra sopesando ambos lados.

origin.text: Participas en un panel sobre movilidad urbana. Escribe en inglés (entre 170 y 250 palabras) tu turno: una apertura con tu postura, una concesión, una refutación con evidencia y un conector formal (hence, thereby, whereby, in so doing) y un cierre con on balance o to sum up.

prompt.es: Lee el extracto. ¿Qué hace el orador con la última frase?

choices.text: He denies that the change has any cost for the shops.
He gives up his support because the change is hard.
He admits that the change has costs yet defends it overall.

feedback.es: «That is not to say the change is easy» concede los costes y «on balance» mantiene su defensa del cambio.

origin.text: My opponent claims that pedestrian streets would empty the centre. The evidence shows the opposite: where they were introduced, the number of visitors rose. That is not to say the change is easy, but on balance the cost is worth paying.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los beneficios de un centro sin autos superan los ingresos perdidos…»

feedback.es: Outweigh significa pesar más que: los beneficios superan el coste.

origin.text: The benefits of a car-free centre ___ the lost parking income, so on balance the plan is worthwhile for the city.

prompt.es: Escucha el cierre y elige qué sugiere la presidenta sobre el debate.

choices.text: That the debate was about solutions, and that she favours a trial.
That the speakers disagreed about whether congestion exists.
That the public should vote on the plan without any trial.

feedback.es: Nadie negó la congestión: el desacuerdo era sobre las soluciones y ella prefiere un plan de prueba a más eslóganes.

origin.audio: The chair closed the panel by thanking the speakers. She noted that nobody had denied the problem of congestion; the disagreement was about how to tackle it, and at what price. In her view, the public would be better served by a trial scheme than by more slogans.
